title: Introduce local-zone egress allocator and DNS stub-bridge for private control plane
author: Rafael Moreno
release_notes: Adds local-zone egress allocator, DNS stub-bridge for conditional cross-zone name resolution, and Terraform/Helm changes to enable zone-affinity egress policies. No user-facing API changes.
description:
Summary: Implements a local-zone-aware egress allocator and a lightweight DNS stub-bridge to improve control plane availability and predictable egress routing for private deployments. This PR adds Terraform modules, Helm chart values, installer hooks, and end-to-end acceptance tests to enable per-zone egress policies and a 'stub-bridge' resolver that forwards selected private DNS zones across VPC peering/subnets with signed verification.

Motivation: Several customers running private control planes across multi-AZ/private VPC footprints reported intermittent control plane failures during AZ-level egress drain and noisy DNS propagation. Existing approaches either forced all control plane egress to a single AZ (bad for resilience) or relied on broad VPC peering + route overlap (fragile for upgrades). The egress allocator aims to pick stable, zone-local egress endpoints with graceful handoff during upgrades, while the DNS stub-bridge provides a minimal, audited path for control-plane-related private DNS queries (controlplane.internal, rpms.redwood-infra) across peered subnets.

What I changed (high-level):
- Terraform: new module modules/egress/local-zone-allocator with CRDs/IGW/ENI allocation logic, route table templates, and IAM policy snippets for signed endpoint approvals.
- Helm: chart/redwood-private/templates/egress.yaml & values.schema.json to toggle zoneAffinity, probe intervals, and dnsStubBridge config.
- Installer scripts: installer/hooks/egress-handshake.sh implements a signed handshake (using customer KMS) when reassigning control plane egress ENIs between subnets to avoid split-brain during upgrade/rollback.
- DNS: add lightweight kubernetes deployment templates for dns-stub-bridge (udp/tcp forwarder, signed-forwarding rules) and config maps for domain routing.
- Tests: e2e/provisioning/test_local_zone_egress.py covers allocation, failover, DNS forwarding correctness, and symmetry during simulated AZ drain.

Operational notes:
- Default behavior is off. Enable via Terraform variable local_zone_egress = true and helm value redwoodPrivate.egress.zoneAffinity = true.
- The signed handshake requires an onboarding step to provision a Customer KMS Key ARN; installer will refuse to activate without it unless run in permissive-mode (not recommended).
- Rollout plan: 1) enable in staging clusters behind feature flags and run e2e smoke; 2) gradual rollout to customer private installs with canary control plane nodes; 3) monitor DNS latency/lookup errors metric namespace 'installer.dns_stub_bridge.*' and egress allocation churn metric 'installer.egress.churn_rate'.

Backwards compatibility and rollback: The changes are additive; disabling zoneAffinity reverts to previous allocator. The installer handshake supports a no-op fallback if signed approval cannot be obtained (controlled by helm flag). Rollback tested in e2e by forcing handshake failures and observing control-plane continuity.

Security: Signed subnet handshakes leverage customer KMS for non-repudiation; the dns-stub-bridge runs constrained RBAC and only forwards for whitelisted domains. Terraform includes least-privilege IAM policies for the allocator.

CI and testing: Initial run failed on integration test flakiness (e2e provisioning timeout). Re-ran the pipeline after increasing the test timeout and pinning aws-sdk to a stable version. Final CI status: all checks passed.

Files changed (representative): modules/egress/local-zone-allocator/main.tf; modules/egress/local-zone-allocator/outputs.tf; chart/redwood-private/values.yaml; chart/redwood-private/templates/dns-stub-bridge-deployment.yaml; installer/hooks/egress-handshake.sh; e2e/provisioning/test_local_zone_egress.py; docs/private-deploy/egress-zone-allocator.md.

Why this is different from prior work: Prior PRs focused on subnet handoffs and conditional DNS forwarding; this PR couples a deterministic egress allocator with a small, signed handshake model and an in-cluster DNS stub-bridge to reduce blast radius and improve observable handoffs during both automated upgrades and operator-led subnet maintenance.

Follow-ups: add a metrics exporter for stub-bridge per-domain latency, and a Terraform data-source for querying allocated egress endpoints for external monitoring systems.

References: ENG-4823 (design doc), SUP-1284 (customer incident), internal RFC: rfc/local-zone-egress-allocator (link in Linear).
